In mathematics, an '''Ockham algebra''' is a [[Bounded lattice|bounded]] [[distributive lattice]] <math>L</math> with a [[duality (order theory)|dual endomorphism]], that is, an operation <math>\sim\colon L \to L</math> satisfying 

* <math>\sim (x \wedge y) ={} \sim x \vee {} \sim y </math>,
* <math>\sim(x \vee y) = {} \sim x \wedge {}\sim y </math>,
* <math> \sim 0 = 1</math>,
* <math> \sim 1 = 0</math>.

They were introduced by Berman,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Berman |first=Joel |date=February 1977 |title=Distributive lattices with an additional unary operation |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF01837887 |journal=Aequationes Mathematicae |language=en |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=118–118 |doi=10.1007/BF01837887 |issn=0001-9054|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and were named after [[William of Ockham]] by Urquhart.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Urquhart |first=Alasdair |date=1979 |title=Distributive lattices with a dual homomorphic operation |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00370442 |journal=Studia Logica |language=en |volume=38 |issue=2 |pages=201–209 |doi=10.1007/BF00370442 |issn=0039-3215|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Ockham algebras form a [[variety (universal algebra)|variety]].

== Examples ==
Examples of Ockham algebras include [[Boolean algebra]]s, [[De Morgan algebra]]s, [[Kleene algebra (with involution)|Kleene algebra]]s, and [[Stone algebra]]s.
